title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): a 'carte triangulaire pondérée' is a map (X,K) on a compact surface. It is a triangulation, a barycentric subdivision, whose vertex set S carries a colouring S → {0,1,∞}. On each face the colouring restricts to a bijection onto {0,1,∞}. The faces are the 'repères' (in modern terms, flags or blades). τ_i is the reflection of a face across its side opposite the vertex of colour i. The group \tilde Π_{03} = ⟨τ_0,τ_1,τ_∞ | τ_i^2⟩ ≅ (Z/2)^{*3} is the extended triangle group of type (∞,∞,∞). Its index-2 subgroup Π_{03} is generated by ρ_∞=τ_1τ_0, ρ_1=τ_0τ_∞, ρ_0=τ_∞τ_1, which satisfy ρ_0ρ_1ρ_∞=1. Π_{03} is free of rank 2, and on the next page it is identified with π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}).

This page:
(i) The figure is the local picture around a base face r. In r, colour 0 is the top vertex, 1 the bottom-left and ∞ the bottom-right. Its three neighbours are τ_∞ r (left, across side 0–1), τ_1 r (right) and τ_0 r (bottom). The six second neighbours are τ_iτ_j r, labelled as rotations: τ_1τ_∞ r=ρ_0^{-1}r, τ_∞τ_1 r=ρ_0 r, τ_0τ_∞ r=ρ_1 r, τ_∞τ_0 r=ρ_1^{-1}r, τ_1τ_0 r=ρ_∞ r, τ_0τ_1 r=ρ_∞^{-1}r. That gives 10 triangles in all, with orientation arrows alternating between adjacent faces. Grothendieck notes that the orientation behaviour is the same as in the figure on p.2' (ordinary maps), but this picture is more symmetric. He also notes that in degenerate cases some of the 10 faces coincide: the octahedron, or the extreme 'universal oriented' case. In that case the Riemann sphere is cut along the real line through 0, 1, ∞ into two triangles (the two hemispheres), and each τ_i swaps them.
(ii) Equivalence (17): finite isotopy classes of weighted triangulated maps ≃ finite 'special' \tilde Π_{03}-sets. 'Special' means the three involutions act without fixed points; a fixed point would be a boundary side.
(iii) Orientation: as for ordinary maps, an orientation of the underlying surface is encoded combinatorially by a subset R^+(X) ⊂ R(X), with R^- = R \ R^+, such that each τ_i exchanges R^+ and R^- (conditions (6 bis)/(7)/(7 bis)).
(iv) This leads (next page, (18)) to the equivalence between oriented weighted triangulated maps and finite Π_{03}-sets, X ↦ R^+(X), with no extra condition.

Purpose: to give the purely group-theoretic and combinatorial description of dessins/Belyi covers as finite Π_{03}-sets (π_1 of the thrice-punctured sphere). Ordinary maps then appear as a full subcategory, via Γ_{32} ≅ \tilde Π_{03}/⟨ρ_1^2⟩. This is the foundation of the Teichmüller/Galois programme.
errors: No mathematical errors. The ten labels in the figure are consistent with (14) (ρ_∞=τ_1τ_0, ρ_1=τ_0τ_∞, ρ_0=τ_∞τ_1) under the left action of words on faces.
Minor gap: (17) tacitly allows non-connected finite maps (finite sets, not transitive ones). This is fine, but connected maps correspond to transitive actions.
Minor gap: 'special' (fixed-point-free τ_i) is only needed because surfaces are taken without boundary. This is not said explicitly here.

ideas.what: Weighted (0,1,∞-coloured) triangulated maps correspond to finite sets with three fixed-point-free involutions, i.e. special \tilde Π_{03}-sets; this covers the non-orientable case.
ideas.modern_name: Non-orientable hypermaps / dessins as actions of the extended triangle group (Z/2)^{*3} on flags; the 'cartographic group'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cori (hypermaps, 1975); Jones–Singerman (1978, maps); Bryant–Singerman (1985, non-orientable maps and boundary); later Shabat–Voevodsky, Jones
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3 (cartes, cartographic groups, Π_{03})

ideas.what: Oriented weighted triangulated maps correspond to finite Π_{03}-sets, Π_{03} being free of rank 2 and equal to π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}).
ideas.modern_name: Dessins d'enfants ↔ finite F_2-sets ↔ Belyi covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); combinatorics in Cori, Jones–Singerman; Belyi (1979) for the arithmetic side

ideas.what: Combinatorial encoding of an orientation as a subset R^+ of flags exchanged with its complement by every τ_i.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation as bipartition of the flag graph (orientable iff the flag graph is bipartite)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in combinatorial map theory (Tutte, Lins, Jones–Singerman)

ideas.what: Local picture of the 10 flags around a base flag as words τ_iτ_j = ρ^{±1}, with degenerations (octahedron; the two-triangle 'universal oriented' sphere).
ideas.modern_name: Flag neighbourhood in the barycentric subdivision; the trivial dessin P^1 → P^1 as the universal oriented object

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful working-out of the standard dictionary between dessins/hypermaps and actions of the (extended) free triangle group. It already appears in Esquisse d'un programme and in the hypermap literature (Cori, Jones–Singerman, Bryant–Singerman). Nothing on the page is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: Figure labels: the involutions are τ (τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞), not π. The left second-neighbour triangle reads τ_0τ_∞ r = ρ_1 r, not 'π_∞π_0 r = ρ_1 r'. The full labels are τ_1τ_∞ r=ρ_0^{-1}r, τ_∞τ_1 r=ρ_0 r, τ_∞ r, τ_1 r, τ_0 r, r, τ_0τ_∞ r=ρ_1 r, τ_0τ_1 r=ρ_∞^{-1}r, τ_∞τ_0 r=ρ_1^{-1}r, τ_1τ_0 r=ρ_∞ r.
In (17) the group is \tilde Π_{03} (with a tilde), not 'Π_{03}^{\mathcal C}'. The left-hand side reads 'cartes isot. triangulées pondérées' (finite).
'certains des 10 [word struck out] les repères de la figure peuvent coïncider': 'repères', not 'régions'.
'R(X) des repères pondérés de X' rather than 'des régions'. Similarly 'R : opérateurs ...' refers to the set of repères.
'(ex: octaèdre, ou complètement plus dégénéré encore, le cas "orient. universel")' is followed by a sketch of the sphere with 0, 1 and ∞ on the equator.
